item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00209","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C14","C02","C24"],"selected_candidate_label":"C14","confidence":0.8,"relationship_type":"both","rationale":"C14 plausibly supplied a reusable response-letter template: acknowledge the correspondent's request, explain that Congress narrowly defined the President's authority, evaluate the request under the national interest, and decline it while identifying the legally available course. The child follows that same sequence and shares unusually close formulations, including an opening acknowledgment, “As you know” followed by a congressional-authority explanation, and a national-interest determination. C02 has notable parallels involving an expiring economic statute, minimum recommended amendments, and necessary congressional action, while C24 concerns a Philippine request whose implementation also requires congressional authorization. Neither matches the child's response structure as closely as C14.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"I have received your telegram of March 17 asking that I increase the Philippine sugar quota.","parent_excerpt":"I have your June twenty-fifth letter suggesting I appoint a board","explanation":"Both begin by acknowledging a dated communication and restating the requested presidential action."},{"child_excerpt":"As you know, the sugar quotas are determined by Congress and any modification would require Congressional action.","parent_excerpt":"As you know, Congress in the Taft-Hartley Act authorized the President, in emergencies affecting the national health or safety, to appoint boards of inquiry","explanation":"Both immediately answer the request by defining the President's authority through congressional legislation."},{"child_excerpt":"to make required replacements from any source when I determine it to be in the national interest","parent_excerpt":"I do not believe it would be in the national interest for me to follow your suggestion.","explanation":"Both frame the availability or refusal of the requested action through a presidential national-interest judgment."},{"child_excerpt":"I regret therefore that it has not been possible for me to comply with the wishes of the Philippine sugar producers.","parent_excerpt":"I do not believe it would be in the national interest for me to follow your suggestion.","explanation":"Each ultimately declines the requested intervention after explaining the governing legal constraint."}]}
